title: From Black-Hole Research to Housing AI: 90% Accuracy in Production Equals Failure
dek: Papers praise LLM systems at 90% success rates; EliseAI processes roughly 60 million housing and medical calls yearly, where 90% reliability means millions of failures, so the team picks between LLM and classical machine learning per problem type instead of betting on one tool.
why: It covers how to select and validate production-grade AI—not generic LLM praise. Information density concentrates on engineering trade-offs and validation methodology in the latter half.
who: Engineers and product leads building enterprise or government AI systems, choosing between LLM and classical machine learning, and assessing production-environment reliability.

points.h: 90% accuracy in production is catastrophe, not a passing grade
points.body: A 90% success rate looks respectable in research papers. But EliseAI handles roughly 60 million housing and medical calls yearly; that 10% error rate translates to millions of failed conversations directly affecting people's lives. This gap between theoretical performance and production consequence drove Mario from theoretical physics into production AI—problem complexity didn't shrink, it grew.

points.h: Not every problem deserves an LLM solution
points.body: Many newcomers treat LLM as a universal tool, but LLM performs poorly where you need determinism—identical inputs must yield identical outputs—and precise probability estimation. EliseAI's tenant-retention predictor is built on proprietary deep neural networks, not LLM, because they have massive historical data; classical machine learning is more accurate and faster. Teams must diagnose the problem first, then pick the tool.

points.h: Each additional nine in reliability is a summit by itself
points.body: Academic papers discuss 90% reliability for LLM as a solid achievement. But EliseAI's 60 million yearly calls mean 90% reliability triggers millions of complaint conversations rippling into real tenant and patient lives. This is the chasm between benchmark and consequence, which is why the team assembled both academics and engineers to obsess over evaluation methodology.

points.h: Small-sample testing reveals nothing about method differences
points.body: Test five or six sample conversations and most approaches look equally good. Run the same methods on a million conversations and their quality diverges sharply. EliseAI applies scientific method to product: systematic evaluation at true scale, not gut feel or handpicked samples.

points.h: Internal benchmarks beat external hype for predicting production
points.body: EliseAI's speech system is entirely self-built, so they own every bottleneck. When new speech-to-text, text-to-speech models, or hyped benchmarks appear online, the team doesn't trust published results. They run it internally against real data immediately. They have already automated to Slack + Kubernetes for experiments and are moving toward full automation.

points.h: Rental automation from search to move-in is already possible
points.body: EliseAI has automated the entire rental chain: browsing listings online, booking viewings, using access codes for AI-narrated walkthroughs, signing the lease, and moving in—all without manual handoff. Maintenance requests are mostly automated too—the AI judges urgency, contacts vendors, schedules visits. The only step requiring human labor is the actual repair work itself, which awaits a robot.

points.h: Subsidized housing represents your highest-leverage automation opportunity
points.body: Healthcare and housing account for roughly 40% of US GDP. That is why EliseAI goes deep rather than broad. The team is now focused on reducing operational costs for subsidized housing—a domain of extreme complexity, highest impact on the most vulnerable, and almost zero automation. Cracking it would directly improve residents' lives.

points.h: Production AI proved harder than fifteen years of black-hole physics
points.body: Mario reflected at the show's close: despite fifteen years researching black holes and string theory, production AI's problem complexity exceeded theoretical physics. He attributes this to AI's pace of change and the requirement that production systems answer for real consequences—a compound difficulty theoretical research never faced.

terms.def: Continued training of an open-source base model on proprietary data to adapt it to a specific domain.
Immediately testing new models against internal production data rather than relying on published external benchmarks.
